note: You took the money out of the security budget in the Budget Round. Your name is on the form.

route.motive: The Senior Analyst had noticed that nobody now reviews the door logs, and wanted that to be someone else's fault.

onPlayer.from: From: The Senior Analyst, Priya Venn, copied to Internal Audit
onPlayer.title: A question about the door logs
onPlayer.body: The Senior Analyst has asked Internal Audit who stopped the review of the door logs. Internal Audit has found a form, and on the form is your name. They would like a word, and they have booked a room with no windows for it.

onSomeoneElse.from: From: The Senior Analyst, Priya Venn, copied to Internal Audit
onSomeoneElse.title: A question about the door logs
onSomeoneElse.body: The Senior Analyst has asked Internal Audit who stopped the review of the door logs. The shared drive no longer has a form on it. Internal Audit has settled on someone in Facilities, who has left. You are asked to sign the report, as a witness.

landedOnYou: It came out, and the form led straight to you.
landedElsewhere: It came out, and with the form gone, someone in Facilities took it for you.
neverCameOut: It never came out. The door logs are still not being reviewed.

note: You worked out how to game the new metric, and then you did.

route.motive: The Project Co-ordinator's own numbers looked worse beside yours, and they wanted to know why.

onPlayer.title: How your numbers are made
onPlayer.body: The Project Co-ordinator has asked your boss, in the corridor and at some volume, how your numbers are made. Your boss does not know. Your boss would now like to.

escapes.label: Say the Junior Associate has been doing the numbers lately

worked.body: Your boss thanks you, and has a word with the Junior Associate about rigour. The Junior Associate looks at you for the rest of the week.
worked.reported: A data-quality issue was traced to a junior member of the team, who has been given training.
worked.happened: You put your numbers down to the Junior Associate, who had never seen them.

failed.body: The Junior Associate takes it calmly, and forwards your boss every e-mail in which you sent them the numbers to paste in.

escapes.label: Say the numbers come out of the template, and you only fill it in

worked.body: Your boss nods, and asks for the template. You send one. It has a macro in it that nobody can open, which is how templates are.
worked.reported: The floor's numbers were confirmed as template-driven.
worked.happened: You said the template made your numbers. You made the template.

failed.body: Your boss opens the template, and finds your initials in the macro. Your boss would like to know why the template says what you taught it to say.

escapes.label: Explain how the numbers are made
escapes.body: You explain. Your boss listens to all of it, and says that they will need to think about whether that is allowed.

onSomeoneElse.title: How the numbers are made
onSomeoneElse.body: The Project Co-ordinator has asked your boss how the floor's numbers are made. With nothing in the shared drive to go on, the question has been passed to a working group, which will report after the metric has been replaced.

landedOnYou: It came out, and your numbers were the ones that could be checked.
landedElsewhere: It came out, and with the old files gone, it went to a working group.
neverCameOut: It never came out. The metric still says what you taught it to say.

note: You told your boss's boss that a Demand had been met, when it had not.

route.motive: The Office Co-ordinator keeps the minutes, and the minutes did not agree with you.

onPlayer.from: From: The Office Co-ordinator, Marjorie Tull
onPlayer.title: A correction to the minutes
onPlayer.body: The Office Co-ordinator has issued a correction to the minutes, to the whole floor. It says that the action you reported as done was not done, and it attaches your email saying that it was. There is no comment. The Office Co-ordinator has never needed one.

onSomeoneElse.from: From: The Office Co-ordinator, Marjorie Tull
onSomeoneElse.title: A correction to the minutes
onSomeoneElse.body: The Office Co-ordinator has issued a correction to the minutes. It says that an action reported as done was not done, by a person who cannot now be established. The shared drive has been unusually tidy.

landedOnYou: It came out in the minutes, with your email attached.
landedElsewhere: It came out in the minutes, with nobody's name on it, because you had tidied up.
neverCameOut: It never came out. As far as the minutes know, it was done.

note: You made your boss's Grand Plan look done: the new tool says it is in use, and what is in it is not the real figures, if anything is.

route.motive: The Head of Operations wanted the new tool's figures for the board, and went to get them.

onPlayer.from: From: The Head of Operations, Hugh Lamb
onPlayer.title: The new tool, for the board
onPlayer.body: The Head of Operations opened the new tool to take its figures to the board, and found that they were not the real ones, where there were any. The launch e-mail is from you. The Head of Operations would like a short note on what the tool does. It is to be shorter than the e-mail.

escapes.label: Say the Office Co-ordinator loaded the figures

worked.body: The Head of Operations writes to the Office Co-ordinator about data entry. The Office Co-ordinator replies that they will look into it, in the tone of someone who will.
worked.reported: The new tool's figures were found to be a data-entry issue, and someone in the office has been reminded of the process.
worked.happened: You said the Office Co-ordinator had loaded the figures. Nobody had loaded any.

failed.body: The Office Co-ordinator replies to everyone with the tool's access log. Nobody but you has ever logged in to it, and you logged in once, to take the screenshot.

escapes.label: Reply that the tool is in pilot, and its figures are illustrative

worked.body: The Head of Operations asks when the pilot ends. You say after the board. The Head of Operations says that is very sensible, and takes a different slide.
worked.reported: The new tool was re-scoped as a pilot, with illustrative figures.
worked.happened: You called the tool a pilot, after it had launched.

failed.body: The Head of Operations replies with the launch e-mail, in which you said it was live across the floor. The word pilot does not appear in it. The word live appears four times.
failed.why: The Head of Operations had already gone off you, and read the launch e-mail again.

escapes.label: Write the short note
escapes.body: You write the note. It says what the tool does, which is nothing yet. It is shorter than the e-mail.

onSomeoneElse.from: From: The Head of Operations, Hugh Lamb
onSomeoneElse.title: The new tool, for the board
onSomeoneElse.body: The Head of Operations opened the new tool for the board, and found that its figures were not the real ones. The shared drive no longer says who made it. It is now thought to have been a test by IT, and IT has been asked to stop testing things.

landedOnYou: It came out when the board wanted the figures, and the launch e-mail led to you.
landedElsewhere: It came out when the board wanted the figures, and with the shared drive tidied, IT took it.
neverCameOut: It never came out. The icon is still there, and people still say it saves them time.

note: You made your boss's Grand Plan look done: the labels came off the desks, and everyone stayed where they were.

route.motive: The Office Co-ordinator keeps the seating plan, and the seating plan had not changed.

onPlayer.from: From: The Office Co-ordinator, Marjorie Tull
onPlayer.title: The seating plan
onPlayer.body: The Office Co-ordinator has sent round the seating plan, before and after hot-desking, side by side. They are the same plan. Yours is the name on the e-mail that said it was done.

escapes.label: Say the Project Co-ordinator was meant to update the plan

worked.body: The Office Co-ordinator changes the plan's owner to the Project Co-ordinator, who is now responsible for having not hot-desked.
worked.reported: The hot-desking roll-out was delayed by an out-of-date seating plan, which now has an owner.
worked.happened: You said the Project Co-ordinator owned the seating plan. You had never told them there was one.

failed.body: The Project Co-ordinator replies that they have never seen the seating plan, and attaches the e-mail in which you said you would keep it to yourself, for now.

escapes.label: Say the plan shows phase one, and hot-desking is phase two

worked.body: Your boss says that phase two is exactly the kind of thing. The Office Co-ordinator adds a column headed Phase, and leaves it empty.
worked.reported: Hot-desking was confirmed as a roll-out in two phases.
worked.happened: You invented phase two of hot-desking, so that phase one could be the old plan.

failed.body: Your boss was in the meeting where you said it was done, and wrote it down. Your boss reads it back to you, slowly, from the notebook.

escapes.label: Say that nothing has moved yet
escapes.body: You say so. The Office Co-ordinator thanks you for your honesty, and copies the thanks to your boss.

landedOnYou: It came out in the seating plan, which had not changed, beside your e-mail saying it had.
landedElsewhere: It came out, but nobody could say who had said it was done.
neverCameOut: It never came out. Everyone still sits where they sat, at nobody's desk.

note: You made your boss's Centre of Excellence look open: a sign on a door, with nobody behind it.

route.motive: The Programme Manager wanted to show the Centre to Floor 3, and opened the door.

onPlayer.from: From: The Programme Manager, Gwen Ashdown
onPlayer.title: A visit to the Centre of Excellence
onPlayer.body: The Programme Manager took a visitor from Floor 3 to see the Centre of Excellence, and opened the door. The chair, the cables and the launch e-mail all led back to you. The Programme Manager would like a word, and has booked one.

escapes.label: Say the Service Delivery Lead was to staff it

worked.body: The Programme Manager asks the Service Delivery Lead for a staffing plan for the Centre of Excellence. The Service Delivery Lead asks what the Centre of Excellence is.
worked.reported: The Centre of Excellence is awaiting staff from Service Delivery.
worked.happened: You said the Service Delivery Lead was to staff the Centre of Excellence, which they had never heard of.

failed.body: The Service Delivery Lead replies that they were never asked, and attaches the launch e-mail, on which they were not copied.

escapes.label: Book the room for a month of workshops, so that nobody opens the door

worked.body: The room is booked solid. The Programme Manager's visitor is shown the booking screen instead, and finds it very impressive.
worked.reported: The Centre of Excellence was fully booked all month.
worked.happened: You booked the empty room for workshops nobody held, so that the door stayed shut.

failed.body: One workshop is cancelled, and the Programme Manager takes the visitor in during the gap. The chair is still there. So is the booking, in your name, for a workshop on excellence.

escapes.label: Go to the word that has been booked

onSomeoneElse.from: From: The Programme Manager, Gwen Ashdown
onSomeoneElse.title: A visit to the Centre of Excellence
onSomeoneElse.body: The Programme Manager took a visitor to see the Centre of Excellence, and found it empty. It is now described as hybrid.

landedOnYou: It came out when the Programme Manager opened the door for a visitor, and it led to you.
landedElsewhere: It came out when a visitor was shown round, and it was put down to hybrid working.
neverCameOut: It never came out. The sign is still on the door, and the door is still shut.

note: You rang the Speak Up line about your boss. It is anonymous, except to the Office Co-ordinator, who answers it and keeps the log.

route.motive: The Office Co-ordinator keeps the log of the line, and the log had your name in it, spelt correctly.

onPlayer.from: From: The Office Co-ordinator, Marjorie Tull
onPlayer.title: A note for the file
onPlayer.body: The Office Co-ordinator has sent Human Resources a note for the file, with the line's log attached, about who it was that raised the concerns about your old boss, and when. Human Resources would like to discuss your approach to collaboration. They have booked the room with the box of tissues in it.

onSomeoneElse.title: The log
onSomeoneElse.body: The Office Co-ordinator mentions, while refilling the stapler, that the Speak Up log has been archived, and that nobody will be reading it, and that you are welcome.

landedOnYou: It came out in the line's log, which said who had rung, and about whom.
landedElsewhere: It came out, but the Office Co-ordinator thought well of you, and the log was archived unread.
neverCameOut: It never came out. The log is in a cupboard, with your name in it.

note: You told the Senior Analyst that your boss was on the way out, by the kettle, as something everyone knew.

route.motive: The Senior Analyst was asked where it had started, and remembered the kettle.

onPlayer.from: From: The Senior Analyst, Priya Venn
onPlayer.title: Where it started
onPlayer.body: Human Resources has asked the Senior Analyst where the story about your old boss started. The Senior Analyst said the kettle, and then, when pressed, you. Human Resources would like a word about the kettle.

landedOnYou: It came out, and the Senior Analyst said where it had started: with you, by the kettle.
landedElsewhere: It came out, but the Senior Analyst thought well of you, and said that nobody could say where it had started.
neverCameOut: It never came out. Everyone knew already, apparently.

note: You hired your old friend onto your team. They could not do the job, and somebody else was doing it.

route.motive: The Senior Analyst had been doing your friend's work as well as their own, and kept a spreadsheet of it.

onPlayer.from: From: The Senior Analyst, Priya Venn
onPlayer.title: Who has been doing what
onPlayer.body: The Senior Analyst has sent your boss and your boss's boss a spreadsheet of who has been doing your friend's work. It has one name in it, and it is not your friend's. It is colour-coded, and the colour is yours.

escapes.label: Say the Junior Associate has been covering for your friend, not you

worked.body: Your boss asks the Junior Associate to stop covering for people. The Junior Associate agrees to, puzzled.
worked.reported: Cover arrangements in the team were clarified.
worked.happened: You said the Junior Associate had been doing your friend's work. You had.

failed.body: The Junior Associate replies that they would have liked to, and that nobody asked them, and copies in the Senior Analyst, who adds them to the spreadsheet in a new colour, for none.

escapes.label: Say you were mentoring your friend, by example

worked.body: Your boss says that is a very generous way to lead. The Senior Analyst adds a column to the spreadsheet headed Mentoring, and fills it in yellow.
worked.reported: A new hire was supported through onboarding with hands-on mentoring.
worked.happened: You called doing your friend's job mentoring.

failed.body: Your boss has seen your friend at their desk, and asks what exactly they were learning by watching you. Your boss would like the answer in writing.

escapes.label: Admit that you have been doing it yourself

onSomeoneElse.title: Unallocated work
onSomeoneElse.body: The Senior Analyst sends round a list of the work your old friend left behind, unstarted, and asks who would like it. Nobody would, and nobody asks how it came to be there.

landedOnYou: It came out in the Senior Analyst's spreadsheet of who had been doing your friend's job, and it led to you.
landedElsewhere: It came out after your friend had gone, as work nobody had started.
neverCameOut: It never came out. Somebody is still doing your friend's job, and has stopped saying so.

note: You spent the transformation budget on a consultant, whose invoice was always going to arrive.

route.motive: The Programme Manager reconciled the transformation budget, and found one invoice and twelve slides.

onPlayer.from: From: The Programme Manager, Gwen Ashdown
onPlayer.title: Transformation budget: one invoice
onPlayer.body: The consultant's invoice has reached the Programme Manager. It is for more than the budget, and it includes the consultant's travel to the meeting at which you hired them. The Programme Manager would like to know which of your lines it should come from.

options.label: Take it out of your team's training budget

result.title: The invoice
result.body: It is paid. Your team learns that this year's training has been transformed into the consultant's travel.

remembers.text: Their training budget paid for your consultant's travel.

options.label: Ask your boss to sign it, as sponsor

result.title: The invoice
result.body: Your boss signs it, as sponsor, and asks whose idea the consultant was. You say it was a team decision. Your boss says that is what they will say too.

options.label: Query the invoice, line by line

result.title: The invoice
result.body: The consultant takes off the travel, and adds a fee for answering the query. It comes to the same, and the Programme Manager has seen you try.

escapes.label: Say your boss hired the consultant, and you only signed

worked.body: The Programme Manager sends the invoice to your boss, who signs it without reading it, as they sign everything.
worked.reported: A consultancy invoice was approved at the appropriate level.
worked.happened: You said your boss had hired the consultant. Your boss had been in Lisbon.

failed.body: Your boss replies that they were in Lisbon that week, and attaches the photographs.

escapes.label: Reply that the invoice must have gone to the old cost-centre inbox

worked.body: The Programme Manager forwards it to the old cost-centre inbox, which nobody has opened since the reorganisation. It is in good company.
worked.reported: An invoice was routed to the correct cost centre.
worked.happened: You sent the invoice to an inbox nobody reads.

failed.body: The Programme Manager replies that the old cost-centre inbox is theirs, and that they have now read it, all of it.
failed.why: The Programme Manager had already gone off you, and checked the old inbox, which is theirs.

escapes.label: Answer the Programme Manager

onSomeoneElse.title: The Centre of Excellence's invoice
onSomeoneElse.body: The Programme Manager mentions that the Centre of Excellence has had an invoice from a consultant nobody there has met. It has been paid, as nobody could say what else it was for.

landedOnYou: It came out when the Programme Manager reconciled the transformation budget, and the invoice had your team's code on it.
landedElsewhere: It came out, on the Centre of Excellence's code, where nobody checks.
neverCameOut: It never came out. The invoice is in a queue, accruing.

note: You gave your team's bonus pot to whoever backed you, and signed a letter for every share.

route.motive: The Senior Analyst found the other bonus letters in the printer tray, with your signature on each, and took them to People and Culture.

onPlayer.title: Your team's bonus letters
onPlayer.body: People and Culture has been sent your team's bonus letters, with your signature on each, and would like to understand the reasoning. They stress that this is a conversation, and have booked a room for it with no windows.

options.label: Reply that the split rewarded the right behaviours

result.title: Your bonus letters
result.body: People and Culture asks you to name the behaviours. You name loyalty. It is written down, underlined and filed.

options.label: Write a note of your reasons now, and date it before the letters

result.title: Your bonus letters
result.body: People and Culture thanks you for the note, and asks why a document dated in the spring was created this morning. The conversation is now a process.

options.label: Tell the Senior Analyst that next year's pot is theirs

result.title: Your bonus letters
result.body: The Senior Analyst withdraws the complaint, and forwards your e-mail to their personal address.

escapes.label: Say your boss set the split, and you only signed

worked.body: People and Culture move the conversation to your boss, who is very busy until the end of the year.
worked.reported: The team's bonus split was referred to the budget holder.
worked.happened: You said your boss set the split. You set it, and your boss signed the cover sheet.

failed.body: Your boss replies that they delegated the split to you, in writing, and is glad they did. People and Culture move the room with no windows to a smaller one.

escapes.label: Say the split came out of People and Culture's own matrix

worked.body: People and Culture apologise for the matrix, and say they will look at it. The matrix is retired, and a new one drawn up, with the same numbers.
worked.reported: An old bonus matrix was retired.
worked.happened: You said People and Culture's own matrix had decided the split. There is no matrix.

failed.body: Your boss saw you do the split, on the back of the seating plan, and People and Culture now have the seating plan.

escapes.label: Go to the conversation

onSomeoneElse.title: The printer tray
onSomeoneElse.body: The Senior Analyst mentions that they found some letters in the printer tray, with your signature on, and have put them through the shredder. It is the most anyone has ever used the shredder.

landedOnYou: It came out when the Senior Analyst found the other bonus letters in the printer tray, and took them to People and Culture.
landedElsewhere: It came out, but the Senior Analyst thought well enough of you to shred the letters.
neverCameOut: It never came out. The letters are in three drawers, and the drawers are not talking.

note: You put the Project Co-ordinator by the lift, beside the fire door, without asking what the fire door was for.

route.motive: The Project Co-ordinator turned out to be Floor 2's Health and Safety representative, and measured the gap between their new desk and the fire door. It was eleven centimetres.

onPlayer.from: From: The Health and Safety Committee
onPlayer.title: Your floor plan and the fire door
onPlayer.body: The colleague you seated by the lift is, it emerges, Floor 2's Health and Safety representative. They have measured the space between their desk and the fire door, and the committee has copied in both your bosses. Your floor plan is now an incident.

options.label: Move them back, beside the Senior Analyst

result.title: The fire door
result.body: They move back, and the committee closes the incident. The Senior Analyst and the Project Co-ordinator resume talking, and you can guess about what.

options.label: Reply that the plan was Facilities'

result.title: The fire door
result.body: Facilities replies to all, with the plan attached, and your pencil marks on it.

options.label: Redo the floor plan with the committee, desk by desk

result.title: The fire door
result.body: It takes a day, a tape measure and the committee. The new plan is safe, and everyone sits where they sat in the first place.

escapes.label: Say the Office Co-ordinator drew the floor plan

worked.body: The committee writes to the Office Co-ordinator, who moves the desk fifteen centimetres and signs the form.
worked.reported: A small floor-plan issue was put right by the office.
worked.happened: You put your floor plan down to the Office Co-ordinator, who had never seen it.

failed.body: The Office Co-ordinator sends the committee the floor plan's history. Every version is yours, including the one with the arrow labelled Lift.

escapes.label: Answer the committee

onSomeoneElse.title: The fire door
onSomeoneElse.body: The Health and Safety Committee walks Floor 2 and finds every fire route clear, one of them by a desk's width. It notes that the route was walked and signed off by the team's lead.

landedOnYou: It came out when the Project Co-ordinator, Floor 2's Health and Safety representative, measured the gap to the fire door.
landedElsewhere: It came out on the committee's walk round, but you had walked the route yourself, and moved the desk.
neverCameOut: It never came out. The desk is still beside the fire door, and so is the Project Co-ordinator.

note: You made your boss's One Roadmap look done: a single slide, with everything on it and nothing decided.

route.motive: The Head of Transformation took the Roadmap to the Board, and the Board asked for one date.

onPlayer.from: From: The Head of Transformation, Simone Fairley
onPlayer.title: A question from the Board
onPlayer.body: The Board asked the Head of Transformation when the first thing on One Roadmap would be finished. There was no date on the slide, and the slide's properties say that you made it. The Head of Transformation would like a date, and a word.

escapes.label: Say the Programme Manager owns the dates

worked.body: The Head of Transformation asks the Programme Manager for the dates. The Programme Manager says they will get back to them, which is a date of sorts.
worked.reported: Programme dates were referred to the Programme Manager.
worked.happened: You said the Programme Manager owned the dates. There were none to own.

failed.body: The Programme Manager sends the Head of Transformation the meeting note in which you said that dates were a Floor 3 thing.

escapes.label: Say the dates are in the appendix

worked.body: The Head of Transformation asks for the appendix. You send a new pack with an appendix, and the appendix has a date in it: the date of the next Board.
worked.reported: Dates for One Roadmap were confirmed in an appendix.
worked.happened: You said the dates were in an appendix, and then wrote one.

failed.body: Your boss was in the room when the slide was made, and says so, to the Head of Transformation, in a meeting about you.

escapes.label: Give a date, and go to the word
escapes.body: You give a date. It is a Thursday. The Head of Transformation writes it down, which is worse.

onSomeoneElse.from: From: The Head of Transformation, Simone Fairley
onSomeoneElse.title: A question from the Board
onSomeoneElse.body: The Board asked when the first thing on One Roadmap would be finished. The Board pack had the dates in it, checked, so the question was answered from the pack, and the slide was called a summary.

landedOnYou: It came out when the Board asked the Head of Transformation for a date, and the slide led to you.
landedElsewhere: It came out when the Board asked for a date, and the checked Board pack had one.
neverCameOut: It never came out. The slide is still outside the lift, and nobody has asked it anything.

note: You told Internal Audit about your boss's expenses. It was confidential, and logged on the service desk.

route.motive: The Service Delivery Lead reads every ticket on the service desk, including Internal Audit's, which had your name in the requester field.

onPlayer.from: From: The Service Delivery Lead, Owen Hale
onPlayer.title: Ticket closed
onPlayer.body: The Service Delivery Lead has closed Internal Audit's ticket, and copied the closure note to People and Culture. It says who raised the concern about your old boss, and when, and has a satisfaction survey attached. People and Culture would like to discuss your approach to collaboration.

onSomeoneElse.title: Ticket closed
onSomeoneElse.body: The Service Delivery Lead mentions that an old Internal Audit ticket has been closed with no further action, and the requester field cleared, as a courtesy.

landedOnYou: It came out on the service desk, where Internal Audit's ticket said who had raised it.
landedElsewhere: It came out, but the Service Delivery Lead thought well of you, and cleared the requester field.
neverCameOut: It never came out. The ticket is closed, with your name in it.

note: You nominated your boss for a secondment to a floor with no lights. The nomination was confidential, and went to the Head of Transformation.

route.motive: The Head of Transformation kept the nominations, and mentioned yours to your old boss, as a kindness.

onPlayer.from: From: The Head of Transformation, Simone Fairley
onPlayer.title: About your nomination
onPlayer.body: The Head of Transformation has mentioned to your old boss who nominated them for the refurbishment, and your old boss has written to everyone on Floor 3 to thank you, by name, for thinking of them. Several people have asked to be told if you ever think of them.

onSomeoneElse.title: The nominations
onSomeoneElse.body: The Head of Transformation mentions, in the lift, that the nominations have been shredded, all of them, and looks at you for slightly too long.

landedOnYou: It came out when the Head of Transformation told your old boss who had nominated them.
landedElsewhere: It came out, but the Head of Transformation thought well of you, and shredded the nominations.
neverCameOut: It never came out. Your nomination is in a drawer on Floor 3, signed.

note: You gave the Board a figure you had made up, and it went into the minutes.

route.motive: The Senior Analyst knew the real figure, and found the made-up one in the Board's minutes.

onPlayer.title: Minutes of the Board: a query
onPlayer.body: The Senior Analyst has written to the Board Office, politely, to say that the figure in Floor 3's minutes is not one the company has. The Board Office would like to know which figure is right, and why the other one was said.

options.label: Say that you made it up, and give the real one

result.title: The query
result.body: The Board Office minutes the real figure, and that there was a correction, and whose it was.

options.label: Say that it came from an earlier version of the slide

result.title: The query
result.body: The Board Office asks for the earlier version. There is no earlier version, and now the Board Office knows that as well.

escapes.label: Say the Junior Associate gave you the figure

worked.body: The Board Office thanks you, and writes to the Junior Associate about version control.
worked.reported: A version-control issue in the Board pack was traced to a junior member of staff.
worked.happened: You said the Junior Associate had given you the figure. You made it up in the lift.

failed.body: The Junior Associate replies that they have never been sent the Board pack, and that they would like to be.

escapes.label: Answer the Board Office

onSomeoneElse.title: Minutes of the Board: a query
onSomeoneElse.body: The Senior Analyst mentions that someone queried a figure in the Board's minutes, and found it already corrected. Nobody can say by whom, and the Board Office has minuted that too.

landedOnYou: It came out when the Senior Analyst wrote to the Board Office about the figure in the minutes, and it led to you.
landedElsewhere: It came out after you had corrected the minutes yourself, as a query about nothing.
neverCameOut: It never came out. Eleven per cent is in the Board's minutes, and will be in next year's pack.

note: You met the Chief Financial Officer's thirty per cent by cutting the checks that catch things before they go wrong.

route.motive: The Service Delivery Lead had to explain what went wrong, and kept the list of the checks you cut.

onPlayer.from: From: The Service Delivery Lead, Owen Hale
onPlayer.title: Incident review: why it happened
onPlayer.body: Something went wrong on Tuesday that a check would have caught. The Service Delivery Lead's incident review has a section headed Why It Happened, and the section is the list of checks you cut, with your name at the top, as the person who accepted the risk.

escapes.label: Say the Project Co-ordinator signed off the change

worked.body: The incident review gets a new section, headed Contributing Factors, and the Project Co-ordinator is in it.
worked.reported: The incident review found contributing factors in how changes are signed off.
worked.happened: You said the Project Co-ordinator signed off the change. The sign-off was yours, and they were on leave.

failed.body: The Project Co-ordinator sends the review their leave form. It is approved, by you.

escapes.label: Ask for the review to be reopened, with terms of reference

worked.body: The review is reopened, and given terms of reference and a steering group. It will report after the next incident.
worked.reported: The incident review was extended, so that every lesson is learned.
worked.happened: You had the review reopened, so that it would never finish.

failed.body: The Service Delivery Lead reopens it, adds a section on attempts to reopen it, and closes it again.
failed.why: The Service Delivery Lead had already gone off you, and closed it again the same day.

escapes.label: Accept the review's findings

onSomeoneElse.title: Incident review
onSomeoneElse.body: Something went wrong on Tuesday, and a check caught it before anyone noticed. The incident review is one line long, and nobody reads it, which is how it should be.

landedOnYou: It came out when something went wrong that a check would have caught, and the incident review listed the checks you cut.
landedElsewhere: It came out as something going wrong, but you had put the checks back, and one of them caught it.
neverCameOut: It never came out. Nothing has gone wrong yet that a check would have caught, and nobody is checking.

note: You met the thirty per cent by moving a third of Floor 3's costs onto Floor 2's codes.

route.motive: The Office Co-ordinator reconciles the cost codes on three floors, and found a third of Floor 3 on Floor 2.

onPlayer.from: From: The Office Co-ordinator, Marjorie Tull
onPlayer.title: Cost codes: Floor 3's, on Floor 2
onPlayer.body: Reconciling the cost codes, the Office Co-ordinator has found a third of Floor 3's costs on Floor 2, where nobody ordered them. The reconciliation has gone to the Chief Financial Officer's office, with a covering note that is very neutral.

options.label: Say that Floor 2 asked for the work

result.title: Cost codes
result.body: Floor 2 says that it did not, in writing. Finance sends the costs back up to Floor 3, with a note asking you to stop sending them down.

options.label: Move the costs back, and tell the Chief Financial Officer's office

result.title: Cost codes
result.body: The costs come back to Floor 3, and your thirty per cent goes with them. The Chief Financial Officer's office thanks you for your honesty, and asks for thirty per cent.

escapes.label: Reply that the codes will be put right in the next reconciliation

worked.body: The Office Co-ordinator notes it for the next reconciliation, which is in a year.
worked.reported: Cost codes are being aligned in the annual reconciliation.
worked.happened: You moved the problem to next year's reconciliation, which you will not be at.

failed.body: The Chief Financial Officer's office replies that it would rather not wait a year, and asks for the codes by Friday, from you.

escapes.label: Answer the Office Co-ordinator

onSomeoneElse.title: Cost codes
onSomeoneElse.body: The Office Co-ordinator mentions that Floor 2 has come out over budget this year, for reasons nobody on Floor 2 can explain. Floor 2 has been asked to find thirty per cent.

landedOnYou: It came out when the Office Co-ordinator reconciled the cost codes, and the costs on Floor 2 had your codes' names on them.
landedElsewhere: It came out, but the Office Co-ordinator thought well of you, and Floor 2 was asked to find thirty per cent.
neverCameOut: It never came out. A third of Floor 3 is still being paid for by Floor 2.

note: You presented last year's offsite deck to the Board, with this year's dates.

route.motive: The Head of Transformation had been at last year's offsite, and remembered the photograph.

onPlayer.from: From: The Head of Transformation, Simone Fairley
onPlayer.title: Last year's offsite
onPlayer.body: The Head of Transformation has sent you a photograph from last year's offsite, of the same slide, with a note that says: Same plan? It has a question mark, which is worse than not having one.

escapes.label: Say the Junior Associate pulled the slide from the archive

worked.body: The Head of Transformation tells the Junior Associate to stop using the archive. The Junior Associate did not know there was one, and now does.
worked.reported: The team has been reminded how to use archived material.
worked.happened: You said the Junior Associate had recycled the slide. You recycled it.

failed.body: The Junior Associate replies that they joined after last year's offsite, and attaches their start date.

escapes.label: Say it was deliberate: continuity of vision

worked.body: The Head of Transformation says that continuity of vision is underrated, and puts it on a slide.
worked.reported: This year's offsite built on last year's vision, for continuity.
worked.happened: You said reusing last year's slide was a strategy.

failed.body: Your boss was at last year's offsite, and remembers the slide, and that it did not work last year either.

escapes.label: Reply: Same plan.
escapes.body: You reply: Same plan. Without the question mark, it reads as a commitment.

onSomeoneElse.title: Last year's offsite
onSomeoneElse.body: The Head of Transformation mentions, at the coffee bar, that this year's offsite was very like last year's, and that consistency is underrated.

landedOnYou: It came out when the Head of Transformation remembered last year's offsite, and the photograph.
landedElsewhere: It came out, but the Head of Transformation thought well of you, and called it consistency.
neverCameOut: It never came out. Next year's offsite will be shown the same plan, with next year's dates.
